note: Corrections to the brief's assumptions: Dounis's 'Absolute Independence of the Fingers' is Op. 15 (2 books), not Op. 1; the Daily Dozen is Op. 20; Dounis has 16 violin opuses in all (12, 15, 16, 18, 20, 21, 22, 23, 27, 29, 30, 33, 35, 36, 37 plus the Chopin Op. 25/6 studies; Op. 25 is for viola). The Carl Fischer 'Dounis Collection' (BF16) reprints Opp. 12, 15, 16, 18, 20, 21, 27, 29, 30 only; Opp. 22, 23, 33, 35, 36, 37 survive as IMSLP scans (Universal, Presser, Mills). Galamian has no separate violin 'Scale System'; the 'Galamian Scale System' used on syllabi (Eastman CMS Levels 4-5) is Part 1 of Contemporary Violin Technique Vol. 1 (Galaxy/ECS 1966), co-authored with Frederick Neumann. Not found: any exercise book by Persinger, Zweig (online only), Havas, Rolland (only beginner/movement books), Brian Lewis or Edward Kreiner; Berkley's Basic Violin Technique and Twelve Bowing Studies are catalogued only in LoC and Open Library. Overlaps with other groups: Fischer Basics/Scales, Barber Scales, Rostal Studie in Quarten and the Whistler/Trott rows are also in exam_boards/german_b or the catalogue; the Faber pages for Harris/Cohen/Collier were reopened and agree with exam_boards. Levels for the many unsyllabused titles (Yost, Bloch, Kneisel, Jacobsen, modern scale books) are judgments from title, scope and publisher wording and are marked low or medium confidence. The O'Connor Method volumes are tune books with lessons rather than exercise books, so keep or drop them as you see fit. LoC records are cited through the LoC SRU service (lx2.loc.gov/sru/lcdb, query bath.lccn=...), because catalog.loc.gov needs JavaScript. Shar Music shows an unofficial difficulty scale; it was used only as supporting evidence. Four web searches used. Pages that were unreachable or blocked: ecspublishing.com, sheetmusicplus, prestomusic, thesoundpost (Cloudflare), violinist.com (connection reset), carisch.com; the Rochester ECMS violin curriculum PDF (2019) was used for the syllabus placements.
